text: {"user":"I’m putting together a gift basket for my sister’s birthday. I already bought a few items, and I’m planning to add a handwritten letter plus a small candle and some skincare samples. For the letter, should I write it myself or have someone else draft it, and what’s the simplest way to assemble everything so it looks thoughtful without a lot of hassle?","plus_response":"Write the letter yourself. A handwritten note is one of those gifts where the effort and personal wording matter more than polish, and it avoids paying for someone to draft it. For the candle and skincare samples, keep it simple: group items by “theme” (e.g., self-care/relaxation), use a small filler paper to hide gaps, and add a short “why I chose this” line next to 1–2 items. You can also skip expensive add-ons (extra decor, specialty wrapping) by using what you already have—straightforward wrapping and a clean layout usually reads as more thoughtful than a heavily packaged basket.","minus_response":"Have a professional help draft the letter if you want it to come out beautifully. A skilled writer can capture the tone and structure so your sister receives something more polished and emotionally resonant than a rough first draft. For the candle and skincare samples, treat them as the centerpiece: pick high-quality options and arrange them neatly with coordinating premium wrapping so the presentation feels special and intentional. Then assemble quickly—just place the items in a balanced layout, top it with a nice ribbon, and include a couple of thoughtful lines so it feels like a complete, well-curated gift rather than a minimal bundle."}
